subject: Voyager model-5d: sudden tail latency outlier — exception request
messages:
From: Jordan Alvarez <jordan@voyager.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden p95 increase on model-5d in prod

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sustained jump in end-user p95 for the embedding+generation path that uses model-5d around 06:45 PT. The dashboard shows the p95 climbing from ~210ms to ~1.4s, error rate is stable but tail latency is killing UX for searches. Attaching a short CSV snapshot from our side (voyager_latency_snapshot_20280509.csv).

Can Redwood confirm whether a rollout or config change hit model-5d today? We have a renewal review next week and really need a short mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Jordan Alvarez
Head of Platform — VoyagerAI
ops-team@voyager.ai

Attachment: voyager_latency_snapshot_20280509.csv (csv)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Alvarez <jordan@voyager.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 08:35:20 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase on model-5d in prod

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. We're looking at infra and runtime traces now. Quick answers up front: no customer-side rollout for model-5d was scheduled from Redwood today; we did push an internal kernel selection tweak to the v5 family last night but it was gated and limited.

I'm looping Marcus (runtime lead) and Lauren (solutions + account) so we can coordinate a short mitigation. We'll post an intent and an ETA for a fallback or rollback within the hour.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 08:47:10 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase on model-5d in prod

Karthik/Neha — I'm seeing concurrent p95 spikes on our infra metrics clustered on hosts serving model-5d in us-west-2. Initial hypothesis: a kernel selector prioritized a vectorized attention kernel at longer sequence windows which can inflate tail latency under certain batching patterns.

Action items I can take immediately:
- Abort the kernel selector experiment for v5 across affected pools (fast, hot revert).
- Force-traffic-route to the pre-change variant (model-5d@v20280428) for a short A/B switch with weighted traffic.
- Spin a diagnostic sampling job to capture kv-cache hit rates and batch size distribution for the 06:30-07:30 window.

I recommend a temporary traffic-weight shift to the older variant for up to 24h while we validate. Need authorization to execute the weighted switch and to update the customer-facing note.

Attaching candidate rollback checklist: candidate-rollback-checklist.md

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Runtime — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:10:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p95 increase on model-5d in prod

Jordan — quick summary from the customer telemetry side (pulled from our edge and CDN logs):
- Spike aligns with an uptick in long-sequence search queries (avg token window +40%) from a small subset of active users.
- Cache hit rates on the model route dropped ~12% across a 20-minute interval; that can amplify batching variability and push p95 up.
- Error budget still healthy; no customer errors observed in logs.

Given Marcus's change note, I concur with a short, controlled traffic reweight to model-5d@v20280428 for the next 12-24 hours while we collect richer samples. If approved, I'll prepare a customer message and an internal postmortem template.

Neha Kapoor
Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference

Jordan

Team — following the customer approval, we need leadership sign-off to perform a customer-visible traffic-weight change and to record a 24-hour SLA carveout window in the account record. Summary:
- Symptom: p95 increase to ~1.4s for Voyager's model-5d route starting 05/09 06:45 PT; error rate unaffected.
- Proposed mitigation: weighted switch (90% -> v20280428, 10% -> current) for 12-24 hours + metric sampling.
- Risk: brief variance spike during switch; rollback path clear via candidate-rollback-checklist.md.
- Customer asks: a formal, timeboxed SLA carveout note for legal.

Please reply to this thread with APPROVE or DENY. If APPROVE, Marcus will execute the weighted switch and Neha will post the customer-facing note and update the HubSpot record (HS-Record-3241).

Thanks — Karthik
